card werk-chat-image-inline  [open]  PROPOSED — not in the map until it is accepted
A pasted image travels inside the chat message, and the server stores it
why: The composer sends one request per message. Carrying the image bytes in that request means a message and its images arrive together or not at all. No image is stored for a message that never reached the server, or for an image the person removed before sending.

To send a message and its images in one step, the page reads each pasted image in the browser. It puts the image bytes, encoded as text, into the same request as the message text, the open card and the tab. Nothing goes to the server at paste time. The server checks every image's type and size before it stores any of them. Then it writes each image to the attachments folder and gives the agent the path of each file (see #werk-shots for the folder, the types and the size cap).

Example:

- The person pastes a 2 MB screenshot and a 25 MB screenshot, and types "Why is this red?".
- The person removes the second chip, because it is over the size cap, and presses Enter.

1. Each paste shows a token, [Image #1] and [Image #2], and a chip. The server has no file yet.
2. Removing chip 2 drops its bytes from the page. The server never sees them.
3. Enter sends one request with the text and the bytes of image 1.
4. The server checks image 1, stores it, and the agent's turn names its path as [Image #1].
5. Had the person sent both images, the server refuses the whole request: it stores no image and starts no turn.

```
paste --> page keeps the bytes (chip + [Image #N])      server: nothing yet
Enter --> page --(text + image bytes + card + tab)--> server
                                                       | check every image (type, size)
                                                       |   one bad -> refuse: no file, no turn
                                                       v
                                       store each file --> attachments/
                                                       |
                                                       +--(turn text: [Image #1] = path)--> agent
```

card img-subagent  [decided]
Read an image directly; use a subagent only for long image loops or a short text fact
why: A Read of a PNG or JPG gives the model a native image block, not encoded text. On the current model families one image costs at most 4,784 tokens, because larger images are scaled down first. A direct Read is cheap. A large context comes from text and tool output, not from a few images.

**Default: read the image directly.** One image costs less than 5k tokens.

**Use a subagent in two cases:**
1. A render-and-check loop that will read more than about 10 images in one session. The images then add up, and the subagent keeps them out of the main context.
2. The agent needs only a short text fact from the image.

**Tell the subagent what to check.** A text report loses visual detail: overlaps, spacing, colors. A subagent with no checklist reports only what it finds notable.

  -> refines         root  We build and fix software with agents in one repeating pipeline.
  <- depends_on      werk-test-visual-judge  What makes a visual test pass

The base64 image data stays server-side in werk-v0—the server decodes it to a PNG and gives Claude only the file path to Read, so the agent never handles raw text encoding. I'll correct the card's ambiguous "encoded as text" wording to reflect this.

Yes. Neither choice costs tokens. With both, the agent gets a path and reads a file. The real costs of an upload at paste time are small:

1. **Orphan files.** A removed chip or an unsent message leaves a file in `.werk/attachments/`. That folder is ignored by git, so the cost is disk space only.
2. **A send during an upload.** It is easy to handle: the chip shows a spinner (`#werk-crash`), and Enter waits for it.

An upload at paste time also has real gains:

- A wrong type or a file over the size cap shows at once on the chip, not at send.
- The server can send the thumbnail back, as `#werk-shots` says.
- The send request stays small.

So the option's `why_not` overstated the case. I correct its wording now, so it does not decide this for you.

The whole process died. The chip rendered an `` before the upload finished, so the browser asked for `/api/image?name=` with no name. `join(dir, '')` is the directory itself, `existsSync` said yes, and `readFileSync` threw EISDIR outside any try block. Node killed the process. Three changes, and each one alone would have stopped it. 1. The whole request handler is wrapped. A failed request answers 500 and the server stays up. 2. /api/image uses `basename` and `statSync().isFile()`. An empty name, a dot, or a traversal all answer 404. Tested. 3. The chip shows a spinner until the upload returns a name, so no request is made without one. The lesson is number 1. The other two are the bug; this one is the class of bug. -> refines werk-shots Paste a screenshot into the composer
